title: Three Dimensional Changes on Nasal Septum and Alveolar Cleft After Maxillary Expansion
brief_summary: This study evaluates, by means of cone beam computed tomography (CBCT), the alterations in the nasal septum and alveolar cleft volume that occur in cleft lip and palate (CLP) patients after rapid maxillary expansion(RME). 40 unilateral CLP patients (mean age, 11.1 ± 2.2 years) with transverse maxillary deficiency that underwent to RME will be evaluated in this investigation. CBCT images were taken prior to RME (T0) and after the removal of the expander (T1), for adequate secondary bone graft surgical planning. The scans will be used to analyze the effects on the nasal septum, anterior and posterior maxillary basal width (MBW) and alveolar cleft volume.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* The inclusion criteria comprehended the presence of unilateral cleft lip and palate, rapid maxillary expansion as an initial part of the orthodontic treatment, and absence of previous orthodontic treatment.

Exclusion Criteria:

* The exclusion criteria were absent maxillary permanent first molars, signs of active periodontal disease, and presence of any additional craniofacial syndrome.
study_population: 40 unilateral cleft lip and palate patients (UCLP) (23 male and 17 female), aging from 8 to 14 years old (mean age of 11.1 years ± 2.2). All subjects were in prepubertal or pubertal stage of maturation based on the cervical vertebrae maturation19 assessed on reconstructed lateral cephalograms generated from CBCT.
